lots.working: keep: lowest (and only) same-item SOLD within 24 months is Langtons 2026 $643; $643 / 1.198 = $536.7, round down to $535 (all-in $640.93). flip: likely resale $643 back through Langtons auction, less an assumed 15% seller commission ($96.45) and about $25 to send the bottle to Langtons = $521.55; / 2.396 = $217.7, round down to $215 (all-in $257.57). lots.guide_summary: 10 sold at Noble Numismatics (all AUD, all page opened, all older than 24 months). The six close comps (trios with or without a plaque, KIA or officer) run $440-2,100; the most comparable trio-plus-plaque groups sold $950-1,800. Category guides run from $120 (single medal) to $4,600-5,500 (famous-event or gallantry groups). 0 unsold, 0 asking. Premium status of Noble 'Prices Realised' not stated. No currency conversion needed.
lots.working: No maximum bid. Every SOLD entry is older than 24 months (the newest, Noble Sale 135, is about April 2024) and none is the same group, since a named group is unique. On the old evidence a complete trio plus plaque with badges and a portrait would sit around $950-1,800 at a specialist sale, and the current Gowans bid is $400 (1 bid), so it looks worth a close look, but the rules do not allow a figure without recent same-item SOLD support.
lots.confidence_reason: Names read clearly on the Star, BWM, Victory rim and plaque, and ten Noble results were opened, but none is the same group and none is inside 24 months. His service record (original No. 3, 11th Bn, commissioned, KIA 10 Aug 1918) comes from search snippets only and is unverified, though the plaque confirms death in service.
lots.condition: Plaque toned with spotting, no obvious edge knocks, reverse plain. Star brassy with wear. BWM toned with light contact marks. Victory rim naming legible, brassy. Ribbons on a perspex stand mount, some fading. Miniatures present. Badges lightly oxidised. Telescope with worn/peeling covering. Portrait in a timber frame, not examined for damage.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 9 Star reverse, read directly: '3 / SGT M. D. BLACK. / 11/BN. A.I.F.' (impressed style consistent with official AIF naming). Photo 5 BWM rim: '2/LIEUT. M. D. BLACK. A.I.F.'. Photos 12-13 Victory rim: '...EUT. M. D. BLACK. A.I.F.' (so also 2/Lieut; the researcher's worry about stripped rank on the Victory looks unfounded, it is just split across two photos). Photo 3 enlarged plaque: 'MATHEW DAVID BLACK' (single T spelling, matching AIF records). Photo 14 AC Military Forces Rising Sun hat badge; photo 15 a second, darker Rising Sun. Portrait caption not legible in the photos. Naming style looks right but cannot be confirmed as original at this resolution.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there a Memorial Scroll, King's message, envelopes or any paperwork with the group? What does the caption on the portrait say? Can the medal naming be inspected at the preview for signs of re-naming? Is there any provenance (family consignment)?
lots.dropped_entries: Noonans 2008 GBP 1,900 (lot 157440): site returns HTTP 403 to us, so it was snippet only, and a 2008 UK sale is too old to use; dropped. All ten Noble prices matched the researcher's claims on the lot pages. Sale months are the researcher's from the Noble sale list and are not shown on the lot pages; I could not confirm them (Noble's catalogue list URL returned 404).
